definition: Permission mode that runs reads, file edits and common filesystem commands (`mkdir`, `mv`, `cp`...) without asking. Suited to iterating on code you're reviewing.
The thinking mode set with `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`: Claude determines when and how deeply to think based on the request. Newer models use it by default.

Manages your organization's members, workspaces, invites and API keys programmatically. It needs an Admin API key (`sk-ant-admin...`), an `org:admin` OAuth token, or an unscoped personal/service account key.
The cycle behind Claude Code and the Agent SDK: Claude evaluates the prompt, calls tools, receives the results, and repeats until the task is complete.
A filesystem-based directory with a `SKILL.md` file (YAML frontmatter and instructions), plus optional scripts and resources Claude uses when relevant.
`allowedTools` auto-approves the listed tools; `disallowedTools` blocks them, even in bypassPermissions mode. Unlisted tools stay available.
Claude is trained on alternating `user` and `assistant` turns. Consecutive turns with the same role in a request are combined into a single turn.
AWS's service for accessing Claude with AWS-native authentication, billing and security boundaries, using the same Messages API shape as Anthropic's first-party API.
The environment variable the Claude client SDKs read your API key from automatically, so code can create a client without passing a key.
The request header that opts in to experimental (beta) features, e.g. `anthropic-beta: BETA_FEATURE_NAME`. The SDKs take beta names through a `betas` parameter and send the header for you.
Environment variable that turns on logging in the Python SDK; set it to `debug` or `info`.
Response headers showing the limit enforced, what remains and when it fully replenishes, for requests, tokens, input tokens and output tokens.
A required request header naming the API version, such as `2023-06-01`.
Request header naming the workspace a request runs in. Required with a multi-workspace API key; optional for other keys. A single-workspace key runs in its own workspace when you omit it.
Each HTTP error has a type: 400 invalid_request_error, 401 authentication_error, 403 permission_error, 404 not_found_error, 429 rate_limit_error.
**Personal** keys act as you, **service account** keys act as a service account, and legacy **workspace** keys belong to a workspace.
Within an API version, Anthropic preserves existing input and output parameters, but may add optional inputs and new output values.
The Python SDK's asynchronous client. It has the same interface as the sync `Anthropic` client, with calls you `await`.
The official SDKs retry transient failures (connection errors, rate limits, 5xx errors) with exponential backoff, twice by default.
Notes Claude Code writes for itself from your corrections and preferences, so it accumulates knowledge across sessions without you writing anything.
Permission mode where a second model, a classifier, reviews Claude's actions instead of you, so long tasks run with background safety checks and fewer prompts.
A `claude -p` flag that skips auto-discovery of hooks, skills, plugins, MCP servers, auto memory and CLAUDE.md, reducing startup time. Without it, `-p` loads what an interactive session would.
Once a batch ends, each request has one result type: succeeded, errored, canceled or expired. Only succeeded results include the message.
The thinking budget in manual extended thinking: at least 1,024 tokens and less than `max_tokens`. It is a target, not a strict cap.
Permission mode that runs everything without asking. Use it only in isolated containers and VMs. Deny rules still block in this mode.
A content-block field marking a cache breakpoint: the prompt (tools, system, then messages) up to and including that block becomes the cacheable prefix.
Usage fields for prompt caching: `cache_creation_input_tokens` were written to the cache; `cache_read_input_tokens` were read from it. If both are 0, nothing was cached.
A partial, time-limited deployment of a change to part of a service (the canary), compared with the rest (the control) to decide whether to continue the rollout.
An Agent SDK callback that decides at runtime on tool calls that permission modes and rules don't settle, such as calls matching an `ask` rule.
When thinking is off, asking Claude to think through a problem step by step, with tags like `<thinking>` and `<answer>` to separate reasoning from output.
Claude Code captures your code's state before each prompt, so you can undo Claude's edits. `/rewind` rolls code and conversation back to a checkpoint.
An API feature that returns the exact document passages supporting each claim. Turn it on with `citations.enabled=true` on each document.
The citation field holding the exact passage Claude cites, returned with its location in the source document.
A Python and TypeScript library giving you the same tools, agent loop and context management that power Claude Code, in a process you operate.
A GitHub Action (`claude-code-action`) that runs Claude Code in your repo's workflows: mention `@claude` in a PR or issue, or run a prompt on any GitHub event.
The web Console through which the Claude API is made available: try the API in the playground and generate API keys in Account Settings.
A pre-built, configurable agent harness that runs in managed infrastructure, built around four concepts: agent, environment, session and events.
A markdown file of persistent instructions that Claude Code reads at the start of every session. Project `./CLAUDE.md` is shared via source control.
Claude through Google Cloud's Agent Platform. Requests are nearly the Messages API, except `model` goes in the endpoint URL and `anthropic_version` goes in the request body.
The `-p` (or `--print`) flag runs Claude Code non-interactively for scripts and CI. It exits 0 on success and non-zero when the run fails.
Claude Code command that starts a new conversation with empty context. To free context but continue the same conversation, use `/compact` instead.
Anthropic's official, general-purpose Messages API clients for Python, TypeScript, C#, Go, Java, PHP and Ruby.
Code-based (fastest, most reliable, but lacks nuance), human (most flexible, but slow and expensive) and LLM-based (fast, flexible, suits complex judgment).

source.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations

definition: A server tool that lets Claude run Bash commands and manipulate files, including writing code, in a secure, sandboxed container: useful for data analysis, calculations and generating files.
A research-preview service that analyzes GitHub PRs and posts findings as inline comments, without approving or blocking. Tune it with `CLAUDE.md` or `REVIEW.md`.
Claude Code command that frees up context by summarizing the conversation so far. You can pass focus instructions for the summary.
Replaces the older turns of a conversation with a summary Claude writes on the server, so you need no summarization code of your own.
An input message's `content` is a string or an array of typed blocks. A string is shorthand for one block of type `text`.
Selectively clearing specific content, such as old tool results, from conversation history as it grows, to save cost, stay within limits and keep Claude focused on what matters.
Strategies for curating and maintaining the optimal set of tokens in a model's context during inference, including everything that lands there besides the prompt.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: The degradation of accuracy and recall as the number of tokens in context grows. More context isn't automatically better.
All the text a model can reference when generating a response, including the response itself: its "working memory", not its training data.
`claude --continue` reopens the most recent conversation in the current directory; `claude --resume` resumes a session by ID or name, or opens a picker.
Fable 5.1: demanding reasoning, long-horizon agents. Opus 5.5: long-running agentic coding, knowledge work. Sonnet 5: speed + intelligence. Haiku 4.5: fastest.
A skill's `SKILL.md` creates a /name command. Custom commands have been merged into skills, and existing `.claude/commands/` files keep working.
A unique ID you give each request in a Message Batch (1 to 64 letters, digits, hyphens or underscores) to match it with its result.
A Markdown file with YAML frontmatter (only `name` and `description` are required) whose body becomes the subagent's system prompt.
Your own function Claude can call: a name, description, input schema and handler, wrapped in an in-process MCP server with `createSdkMcpServer`.
Controls where your data is processed and stored. **Inference geo** sets where model inference runs, per request through the `inference_geo` parameter or as a workspace default.
**Disable** is reversible (status `inactive`; Re-enable restores it). **Delete** is permanent: the key is archived.
Skill frontmatter that hides a skill from Claude until you invoke it with `/<name>`; for these user-only skills, nothing loads until then.
Permission mode that allows only file reads in your working directories and pre-approved tools; anything that would prompt is denied. Suited to locked-down CI and scripts.
Two ways to pick a starting model: fast and cheap (Claude Haiku 4.5), upgrading only if needed, or strongest (Claude Opus 5.5), optimizing down.
Controls how many tokens Claude spends responding, from low through medium, high and xhigh to max. It affects text, tool calls and thinking.
Numerical representations of text that let you measure semantic similarity, used for search, recommendations and anomaly detection.
A set of test cases designed to measure an LLM application's performance against clearly defined success criteria.

source.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations

definition: Clear targets that eval results are judged against, such as 95% accuracy, set so you can tell what counts as a good result.
A workflow where one LLM call generates a response while another provides evaluation and feedback, in a loop.
The browser interface for server-sent events: it opens a persistent HTTP connection and receives events in `text/event-stream` format until `close()` is called.
An LLM risk: damaging actions performed in response to unexpected, ambiguous or manipulated model output. Root causes: excessive functionality, permissions or autonomy.
The blocking exit code for command hooks: on events that can block, it stops the action, and `PreToolUse` blocks the tool call.
Scheduling retries with exponentially growing waits. Google SRE says to always randomize the delays, so a brief blip doesn't make clients retry in sync, and to limit retries per request.

Claude works through a problem before answering, returned in `thinking` blocks billed as output tokens. Strictly, **extended thinking** is the manual mode (`type: "enabled"` + `budget_tokens`); newer models use adaptive thinking.
A research-preview option giving up to 2.5x higher output tokens per second on supported Opus models at premium pricing. Opt in with `speed: "fast"` plus its beta header.
A JSON file of end-to-end feature requirements, all initially marked failing, that coding agents update only by changing each feature's `passes` field.
Putting a few well-crafted examples in the prompt: one of the most reliable ways to steer Claude's output format, tone and structure.
Uploaded files can't be modified or renamed. They persist until you delete them or they reach an optional `expires_at`, set once at upload.
Upload a file once, get a `file_id`, and reference that ID in Messages requests instead of re-uploading the content each time.
Creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history, with its own session ID. The original stays unchanged. It branches history, not files on disk.
SDK helpers that stream internally and return the complete Message object: `.get_final_message()` in Python, `.finalMessage()` in TypeScript.

When a language model generates text that is factually incorrect or inconsistent with the given context. Mitigations include allowing uncertainty, grounding answers in direct quotes and verifying with citations.
A lightweight model, such as Claude Haiku 4.5, that pre-screens user input before it reaches your main conversation.
Lets organizations process protected health information (**PHI**) through eligible Claude API features, with a signed BAA. Processing PHI in the Claude Console isn't covered.
User-defined shell commands that Claude Code runs automatically at specific points in its lifecycle, such as after a tool call (`PostToolUse`).
An HTTP method is idempotent if one request has the same intended effect on the server as several identical ones. Safe methods, PUT and DELETE are; POST and PATCH aren't guaranteed to be.
An `image` content block's source can be base64 data, a URL to a hosted image, or a `file_id` from the Files API.
An attack where the user is trusted but Claude processes third-party content (web pages, emails, documents, tool results) with adversarial instructions.
The first session of a long-running harness: it sets up an `init.sh` script, a `claude-progress.txt` log and an initial git commit.
The delta type for a streamed `tool_use` block: partial JSON strings that build up the tool's `input`.
An optional `tool_result` field: set it to `true` when the tool execution resulted in an error, with the error message in the content.
MCP flag on a tool result reporting a **tool execution error** (API failure, bad input, business logic) so the model can self-correct and retry, unlike a protocol error.
For most Claude models, only uncached input tokens count toward input-tokens-per-minute (ITPM) limits; tokens read from cache don't.
An attack where the user of your application is the adversary, crafting inputs meant to bypass your guardrails.
The structured outputs mode that constrains Claude's response to a JSON schema you supply, using constrained decoding.
The message format of MCP's data layer: clients and servers exchange JSON-RPC requests, responses and notifications for discovery and for primitives such as tools, resources and prompts.
An agent keeps lightweight identifiers (file paths, stored queries, web links) and uses tools to load the data into context at runtime.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: A low-level orchestration framework and runtime for long-running, stateful agents, mixing deterministic steps and LLM-driven steps in one graph, with durable execution and human-in-the-loop.
Giving each tool, extension or agent only the permissions it needs, and acting on downstream systems as the specific user, to limit the scope of harmful actions.

Settings your organization deploys to every developer's machine. Claude Code applies them above every other level, so user, project, local or `--settings` values can't override them (bar a few security exceptions).
If one API request contains more than 20 images, a stricter per-image dimension limit applies to every image in that request.
A catalog of plugins: a directory or repository with a `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` file listing each plugin and where to fetch it. Users register it, then install plugins from it.
The maximum number of tokens to generate before stopping. The model may stop **before** reaching it; it is only an absolute ceiling on output.
Agent SDK caps on tool-use turns and on spend. Hitting one ends the loop with an `error_max_turns` or `error_max_budget_usd` result.
A component inside the MCP host that maintains a dedicated connection to one MCP server and obtains context from it for the host to use.
A beta Messages API feature that connects to remote MCP servers without a separate MCP client: servers in `mcp_servers`, each used by one `mcp_toolset`.
The AI application, such as Claude Code or an IDE, that coordinates MCP clients. It creates one MCP client for each MCP server it connects to.
The file at the project root that holds project-scoped MCP servers. Check it into version control so everyone on the team gets the same MCP tools.

source.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP

definition: A program that exposes capabilities to AI apps through the Model Context Protocol, using three building blocks: **tools**, **resources** and **prompts**.
**Local** (the default; this project, private), **project** (`.mcp.json`, shared via version control) and **user** (all your projects, private).

source.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP

definition: On by default: only MCP tool names and server instructions load at session start, and full tool schemas are deferred until Claude needs a tool.

source.title: Connect Claude Code to tools via MCP

definition: **stdio**: standard input/output between local processes on the same machine. **Streamable HTTP**: HTTP POST plus optional SSE, enabling remote servers.
An Anthropic-provided, client-side tool: Claude requests file operations under `/memories`, and your application executes them on storage you control.
Asynchronous processing of large volumes of Messages requests at 50% lower cost. Most finish in under 1 hour; unfinished batches expire at 24 hours.
The token counts in the `usage` field of a streaming `message_delta` event. They are **cumulative**.
A Messages API response: role assistant, `content` as an array of typed blocks, and fields such as `stop_reason`, usage, id and model.
Microsoft's platform for accessing Claude models with Azure-native endpoints and authentication; usage is billed through the Azure Marketplace.
When receiving a streaming (SSE) response, an error can occur after the API has already returned a 200 response.
On the Claude API, a short name for a pre-4.6 model, such as `claude-sonnet-4-5`, that points to the most recent dated snapshot for that minor version.
**MCP**: an open-source standard for connecting AI applications to external systems such as data sources, tools and workflows.

source.title: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?

definition: A stop reason on Claude 4.5 models and newer: generation stopped because it reached the context window limit.
**Active** (fully supported), **Legacy** (no more updates), **Deprecated** (still works; has a replacement and retirement date), **Retired** (requests fail).
Claude base prices are per million tokens (MTok), set separately for input and output, e.g. Claude Sonnet 5: $2 input, $10 output.
A multi-agent design: a lead agent plans the work, spawns subagents that explore in parallel with their own context windows, then synthesizes their findings.

source.title: How we built our multi-agent research system

definition: Identical inputs may produce different outputs across API calls. Even with temperature set to 0, results are not fully deterministic.
A standard authorization flow a client uses to establish that a user is authorized to access a remote server. MCP follows OAuth 2.1 conventions for remotely hosted, HTTP-based servers.
The Agent SDK can export metrics, log events and traces (beta) over OTLP. It's off until you set `CLAUDE_CODE_ENABLE_TELEMETRY=1` and choose an exporter.
A workflow where a central LLM dynamically breaks down a task, delegates subtasks to worker LLMs and synthesizes their results.
Output-tokens-per-minute rate limit. It counts only the tokens actually generated, in real time; `max_tokens` doesn't factor in.
A `claude -p` flag controlling output: `text` (default), `json` (result, session ID and metadata) or `stream-json` (newline-delimited JSON for real-time streaming).
A set of instructions that sets Claude's role, tone and response format for every response in a Claude Code session. Four built-in styles exist besides the default; you can write your own.
The API is temporarily overloaded. 529 errors can occur when the API experiences high traffic across all users.
The OWASP GenAI Security Project publishes the Top 10 for LLM Applications: the main risks, vulnerabilities and mitigations for developing and securing generative AI and LLM apps.
LLMs work on a task simultaneously and outputs are aggregated programmatically. **Sectioning** splits independent subtasks; **voting** repeats the same task.
By default, Claude may return several `tool_use` blocks in one response. You choose how to run them: concurrently, sequentially or in any combination.
Sets which actions Claude can take in a session without asking first: `default` (Manual), `acceptEdits`, `plan`, `auto`, `dontAsk` or `bypassPermissions`. Deny rules apply in every mode.
Allow, ask or deny rules for tools, such as `Bash(aws s3 ls)`. Evaluated deny, then ask, then allow; the first match wins, so a deny always beats a narrower allow.
**Personal identifiable information**: data that identifies a person. OWASP lists it among the sensitive data an LLM app can disclose, alongside financial, health and credential data.
Each Claude model ID is a pinned version: the model stays constant for that ID's lifetime. From the 4.6 generation on, IDs are dateless, e.g. `claude-sonnet-5`.
A permission mode in which Claude researches and proposes changes without making them: it reads files, explores and writes a plan, but doesn't edit your source.
A directory of skills, agents, hooks, MCP servers or other components that Claude Code installs and loads as one unit, usually with a `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` manifest.
An optional file at `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` carrying a plugin's metadata; `name` is the only required key.
A written record of an incident: its impact, the actions taken, the root causes and follow-up actions to prevent recurrence. Google SRE practice is to keep postmortems blameless.
The Claude Code hook event that fires after a tool call succeeds.
A partial assistant message on the last turn for Claude to continue from. Not supported starting with Claude 4.6 models: those requests return a 400.
An Agent SDK hook callback that fires before a tool executes and can allow, deny or modify the call, for example by returning a deny decision.

source.title: Intercept and control agent behavior with hooks

definition: Initial training on a large unlabeled text corpus. Autoregressive models like Claude's underlying model learn to predict the next word from prior context.
Skills load in stages: metadata always (about 100 tokens per Skill), the SKILL.md body when triggered (under 5k tokens), bundled files only as needed.
An API feature that lets a request resume from a previously processed prompt prefix, reducing processing time and cost for prompts with repeated content.
A workflow that splits a task into a sequence of steps, each LLM call processing the previous output, with optional programmatic checks (gates) between steps.
A vulnerability where inputs alter an LLM's behavior or output in unintended ways. The input need not be human-visible, as long as the model parses it.
Exposure of sensitive information you expect to stay hidden in your prompt, such as a proprietary formula in the system prompt.
A Python AI SDK from Pydantic: a typed, extensible agent loop where switching to another model is a string swap.
**Retrieval augmented generation**: relevant documents are retrieved from an external knowledge base at query time and passed into the context window, grounding the response in evidence.

The maximum number of API requests an organization can make over a period, measured per model class in requests (RPM), input tokens (ITPM) and output tokens (OTPM) per minute. Exceeding one returns a 429.
A deny rule such as `Read(./.env)` that blocks Claude's file tools, recognized Bash file commands and redirections from reading a path.
Re-sending a request that came back with `stop_reason: "refusal"` to another Claude model, which can usually still answer it.
A unique identifier on every API response, sent in the `request-id` header and in error response bodies as `request_id`.
Maximum request size per endpoint: 32 MB for Messages and Token Counting, 256 MB for Message Batches, 500 MB for the Files API.
Sent with a 429 rate-limit error: the number of seconds to wait until you can retry the request. Earlier retries will fail.
Setting a role in the system prompt, such as "You are a helpful coding assistant specializing in Python", to focus Claude's behavior and tone.
A workflow that classifies an input and directs it to a specialized follow-up task, such as a different prompt, tool set or model.
In Claude Code, an OS-enforced boundary around the shell commands Claude runs: you set which files and network domains they can reach. It's off by default; turn it on with `/sandbox`.
A content block (`type: "search_result"`) for your own retrieved content, so Claude can cite it the way it cites web search results, with the source and title you provide. Used in RAG apps.
**SSE**: a way for a server to push new data to a web page at any time over HTTP, as a stream of events, instead of the page asking for each update.
Client tools (yours, plus Anthropic-schema tools such as `bash`) run in your application. Server tools (such as `web_search`) run on Anthropic's infrastructure.
Agent SDK option choosing which filesystem settings load (user, project, local, plus CLAUDE.md and `.claude/` files). Omitted: same as the CLI. `[]`: none of them.

source.title: Use Claude Code features in the SDK

definition: Highest first: managed, command line, project local, shared project, user. A key set at a higher level overrides the same key lower down.
Four scopes: **user** (you, all projects), **shared project** (committed, whole team), **project local** (you, one project), **managed** (your organization).
A 429 `rate_limit_error` returned once your organization reaches its tier's monthly spend cap. It has no `retry-after` header.
The Messages API keeps no conversation state between calls: you always send the full conversational history with each request.
A rule that ends an agent loop even if the task isn't finished, such as a maximum number of iterations.
A response field saying why Claude stopped, e.g. `end_turn` (finished naturally) or `max_tokens` (hit your limit).
A Messages API parameter: custom text sequences that make the model stop generating when it encounters one of them.
An open-source toolkit for building AI agents in Python and TypeScript (agent harness and SDK). Agents run in-process; Amazon Bedrock is the default model provider, with others available.
Recovering an interrupted stream: save the content received before the error, then send a continuation request so Claude resumes.
`message_start`, then each content block (start, one or more deltas, stop), then one or more message deltas, then a final `message_stop`.
Setting `"stream": true` on a Messages request returns the response incrementally as server-sent events (SSE).
Setting `strict: true` on a tool definition constrains sampling so Claude's tool inputs strictly follow the tool's `input_schema`.
The agent regularly writes notes to memory outside its context window; the notes are pulled back into context at later times.

source.title: Effective context engineering for AI agents

definition: Constrains Claude's responses to a schema so output is valid and parseable. Two features: **JSON outputs** (`output_config.format`) for the response, and **strict tool use** (`strict: true`) for tool inputs.
A specialized assistant that handles one kind of task in its own context window, with a custom system prompt, specific tool access and independent permissions, and returns only a summary.
A non-fork subagent starts fresh: its own system prompt plus the Agent tool's prompt, without the parent's history. Only its final message returns.
What a lead agent gives each subagent: an objective, an output format, guidance on the tools and sources to use, and clear task boundaries.

source.title: How we built our multi-agent research system

definition: The measurable targets an LLM app must meet. Good criteria are **specific**, **measurable**, **achievable** and **relevant** to the app's purpose and users.

source.title: Define success criteria and build evaluations

definition: The top-level Messages API field for instructions that apply from the start of a conversation, such as a goal or role.
A parameter that controls the randomness of a model's predictions during text generation.

The `display` field of the thinking config. `"summarized"` returns a summary of Claude's reasoning; `"omitted"` (the default on many models) returns thinking blocks with an empty `thinking` field. Billing is the same.
The time from sending the prompt until the model generates the first token of its response.
The smallest unit a language model works in: a word, subword, character or byte. The glossary puts a Claude token at approximately 3.5 English characters.
The algorithm the API uses for rate limiting: capacity is continuously replenished up to your maximum, rather than reset at fixed intervals.
`POST /v1/messages/count_tokens` returns an input-token estimate for Messages inputs, except most server tools, the MCP connector and URL or file sources.
Optional MCP hints about tool behavior, e.g. `readOnlyHint` (doesn't modify its environment) or `destructiveHint`. Clients must treat them as untrusted unless the server is trusted.
A request field that controls tool calling: **auto** (Claude decides), **any** (must use one of the tools), **tool** (must use the named tool) or **none**.
A user-defined tool entry: a **name** matching `^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$`, a detailed plaintext **description**, and an `input_schema` (a JSON Schema object).
The content block your app sends on the next request with a tool's output, answering a `tool_use` block. Claude never sees your implementation, only the schema and the result.
A context editing strategy, `clear_tool_uses_20250919`, that clears the oldest tool results once context passes a threshold, leaving placeholder text.
A beta SDK helper that runs your tools when Claude calls them, sends results back and manages conversation state until Claude stops calling tools.
Lets Claude work with hundreds or thousands of tools: tools marked `defer_loading: true` stay out of context until Claude searches the catalog and loads only the ones it needs.

Lets Claude call functions you define or Anthropic provides. Claude decides when to call a tool from the request and the tool description, then returns a structured call that your app (client tools) or Anthropic (server tools) runs.
The response content block Claude emits to call a tool: the tool name plus a JSON object of arguments. Your app runs the operation and sends the output back in a `tool_result` block.
A hook output field: in a `PreToolUse` hook it replaces the tool's arguments before the tool runs.
The Claude Code hook event that fires when a prompt is submitted, before Claude processes it.
A server tool that lets Claude retrieve the full content of specified web pages and PDF documents. You pay only standard token costs for the fetched content.
A server tool giving Claude real-time web content, so it can answer with up-to-date information beyond its knowledge cutoff. Responses include citations for the sources used.
An API for a two-way interactive session between browser and server: either side can send messages without the client polling for replies.
**Workflows** run LLMs and tools through predefined code paths. **Agents** let the LLM dynamically direct its own process and tool use.
A way to organize API usage within an organization, separating projects, environments or teams while keeping centralized billing and administration.
A request header carrying your API key from the Console. It is the legacy fallback for the `Authorization: Bearer` header, and is still supported.
Wrapping each type of prompt content in its own tag, such as `<instructions>` or `<context>`, so Claude can parse a complex prompt unambiguously.
**ZDR**: an arrangement under which Anthropic doesn't store prompts or responses at rest after the API response returns. Enabled per organization, for eligible features only.
